customer_xyz: Hi — a customer hit our rerank endpoint with ~120 docs and got a 413 and then when they retried some calls returned all 0.0 scores. They say the error message is "413 Payload Too Large" but it's confusing because when it returns 200 the ranking is flat. Any ideas?
eli_support: Ugh, thanks for flagging. Do we have the original request body or a sanitized sample?
customer_xyz: Pasting a small repro they sent (sanitized):
customer_xyz: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.dev/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"What are the license terms for the dataset?","documents":["<very long doc text... ~6-7k chars>","<very long doc text...>","...repeat x120..." ]}'
```
customer_xyz: They estimated ~700 tokens per document, ~120 docs, query ~120 tokens.
eli_support: Ok that's huge (~84k tokens). Our rerank token ceiling per request is documented but the error UX for customers isn't very clear. Also flat scores could be from truncated inputs or an internal fallback.
aaron_backend: I can dig in. Quick note: if the request exceeds the server-side token limit we sometimes stream back a 413, but if the proxy truncates body and the runtime sees empty passages it can return default scores (0.0) instead of an explicit error — bad UX.
maria_prod: @aaron_backend can you confirm which component returns the 413 vs which returns flat scores? We need to surface correct error text to users and suggest automatic chunking.
aaron_backend: Verified: load-balancer rejects bodies > 8MB with 413. Separately the reranker runtime expects non-empty passages; if all docs get truncated to empty strings due to client-side trimming or incorrect encoding, model returns uniform scores (we saw this in recent logs). So two pathways.
eli_support: OK, actionable items: 1) share a reproduction curl we can run, 2) ask customer to try batching (e.g., 20 docs per call), or send only doc snippets (first 2-3 passages) and use search pipeline prior to rerank.
customer_xyz: They asked for a concrete example of chunking.
eli_support: Suggested example: split into batches of 20 docs and call rerank sequentially, then merge top-k across batches. Also recommend trimming document fields to a 'passage' field — don't send whole full-text if you only need short passages.
eli_support: Example message for customer to try (short): "Try sending 20 docs per request and include the top 256 token snippet for each doc. If you still get 413, fall back to client-side chunking and retry with smaller batches."
customer_xyz: They ran a quick test with 20 docs (each ~700 tokens) and got 200 but scores still looked odd (mostly identical).
aaron_backend: If scores are identical after successful 200s, let's check whether the documents were truncated on our side or whether the model input encoding resulted in identical embeddings. Can you share one of the 200 responses?
customer_xyz: Sent a sample response (sanitized). It contains scores like [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, ...] and a warning in headers: X-Processed-Docs: 0.
eli_support: X-Processed-Docs: 0 is a smoking gun — that means the reranker didn't receive valid passages. Either the JSON field names didn't match or the base64/html encoding stripped content.
aaron_backend: Confirmed in logs for that customer: some doc payloads had unescaped null bytes and the JSON parser dropped them -> bodies became empty arrays. We added logging: parsing_errors: true for that session id.
maria_prod: For UX fix: we should change 413 response body to include our token ceiling and a hint: "reduce doc count or trim doc length; try 20 docs/batch or send passages instead". Also add header X-Token-Ceiling: <N>.
eli_support: Agreed. For immediate customer help we should: 1) explain root cause (body too big / invalid JSON -> empty docs -> flat scores), 2) provide concrete repro curl and chunking example, 3) offer a script snippet to count tokens client-side before sending.
eli_support: Quick token count snippet suggestion (pseudo):
eli_support: ```python
# rudimentary token estimate for customer
def estimate_tokens(text):
    return len(text.split()) * 1.3  # rough heuristic, not exact
```
customer_xyz: Also wants to know why the error message didn't mention token limits. They said the 413 just showed "payload too large" with no guidance.
aaron_backend: We'll push an immediate doc patch + API error payload update. For now tell customer: "413 = request body too large for proxy (try smaller batches). If you receive 200 with flat scores, send us the X-Processed-Docs header value and a sample response body so we can check parsing errors."
maria_prod: I'll file a small ticket to add X-Token-Ceiling and clearer message text and also add a KB entry with examples: chunking, snippeting, pre-filtering via embeddings.
eli_support: Thanks all. customer_xyz, I'll DM you a ready-to-run curl that does 20-doc batches and shows how to merge top-5 results across batches. If they want, we can also run a one-off private scan of their payload to show where nulls are introduced. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Note: ticket #INC-2026-317 created for API error messaging improvements (assign: eng-runtime).
